confidence_notes: I ran 5 web searches: 1 for the RBA rate and 4 for food and drink prices. Beer, coffee, inexpensive meal and mid-range meal for two are based on aggregated, partly crowd-sourced cost-of-living indexes (Numbeo-derived and similar). These disagree somewhat: beer about $1.93-2.72, cappuccino about $2.3-3.2, inexpensive meal about $2.3-3.2, mid-range meal for two about $19-23 (about KES 2,500-3,000). I set the anchors modestly above the index averages, because the target is a restaurant serving rather than street or local-bar pricing. Cocktail and wine rest mainly on a few Mombasa venue listings in tourist areas such as Nyali (cocktails about $4.50-9, wine about $3.75-7 per glass, beer about $2.25-4). I did not find an aggregated index for these, so I anchored them to the local beer price relationship and the venue ranges. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge of Mombasa's coastal tourism market. No accommodation searches were done and no live listings were inspected. Hotel prices are seasonal, and beach-resort 3-star rates can be well above city-centre 3-star rates; I assumed a mid-point. The searched food and drink data are current to late 2026, not specifically July 2026.
comparable_city_reasoning: Mombasa is a coastal Kenyan tourism hub. Its restaurant prices are lower than Nairobi's, which one comparison puts about 21% higher. Its price level is similar to other East African coastal and secondary tourist cities, such as Zanzibar town or Dar es Salaam, which sit at the lower end of tourist-priced Africa.
